**Method of record (unchanged from the previous run)**

- **Element**: Chain source · **Rule used today**: Cboe delayed-quote CDN, primary (one JSON per underlying, 1.1–3.2 MB each)
- **Element**: Cross-check · **Rule used today**: Nasdaq `/info` `secondaryData` for the official close (8/8 HTTP 200); Yahoo options chain for the expiry list, implied vol and the `inTheMoney` flag
- **Element**: Pre-cut rule · **Rule used today**: Per-underlying top-10 by volume (`min_volume=100`), NOT the self-referential V/OI cut
- **Element**: Ranking · **Rule used today**: Kept set ranked by V/OI descending; top 25 published, top 10 headlined
- **Element**: Filters · **Rule used today**: V/OI ≥ 1.0, volume ≥ 200, DTE ≤ 60
- **Element**: Bias tag · **Rule used today**: put/call ratio < 0.85 → CALL, > 1.20 → PUT, otherwise MIXED (the series convention used on 2026-10-28, -29 and -30)
- **Element**: Moneyness · **Rule used today**: Side-aware: a call is ITM below spot, a put above spot

- **Headline read: CALL.** The kept set puts **1,281,881 call contracts against 900,829 put contracts — a put/call ratio of 0.70 — and the call lean survives every structural cut:
- it holds with IWM removed (0.59), with same-day expiries removed (0.57), with both removed (0.58), on the OI ≥ 50 floor (0.70), and on the cleanest slice (OI ≥ 50, ex-IWM, ex-0DTE, 0.58).
- Seven of the eight underlyings read CALL on their own kept rows; only IWM is balanced (0.92).

- **By contract count the day is call-leaned; by premium dollars it is too.** The theoretical premium implied by the kept set is $1,059,452 of calls against $876,976 of puts —
- a put/call premium ratio of 0.83. The one slice that is not call-leaning is the economic-flow cut (theo ≥ $0.05, 0.95, MIXED):
- once the zero-premium prints are removed, the surviving 57 rows are close to balanced by contract count, and only the ex-IWM, ex-0DTE economic slice (0.59) restores the lean.
- The read is therefore *broad but shallow* on the call side: the call-heavy contracts are mostly cheap ones.

- **Contract-count is not economic size.** 27.5% of kept volume (600,232 of 2,182,710 contracts) sits in contracts with a theoretical value below $0.05 — real contracts, trivial premium dollars.
- That share is far below the 54.0% recorded on 2026-11-02 and the 49.5% on 2026-10-30: **today's book is materially more economically meaningful than the two preceding sessions.**

- **Contrast with the skill-literal V/OI pre-cut.** Had the per-underlying ten been cut by V/OI instead of volume, the kept set would be 70 rows carrying 1,274,173 contracts (vs 2,182,710 under the method of record) and the put/call ratio would read 0.69 —
- CALL, the same direction as the headline. Published as contrast, not as the answer.

**IV reliability (Cboe column vs Black-Scholes inversion of the mid-quote)**

- The Cboe `iv` column was checked against an inversion of each contract's own mid-quote (r = 3.85%, q = 0.5%, side-aware call/put branch, no-arbitrage clamp).
- **71 of 73 rows** were invertible. The median gap is **0.8 vol points**, but the error is not spread evenly:
- **15 of 70 rows diverge by more than 10 vol points, and every one of them is a 0DTE IWM or GLD contract priced at a penny with a wide bid-ask.**

- **Contract**: IWM261103C00284000 · **Cboe IV**: 123.6% · **Inverted IV**: 13.0% · **Gap**: 110.6pp (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Contract**: GLD261103C00365000 · **Cboe IV**: 117.4% · **Inverted IV**: 13.3% · **Gap**: 104.2pp (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Contract**: IWM261103C00283000 · **Cboe IV**: 99.1% · **Inverted IV**: 10.3% · **Gap**: 88.8pp (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Contract**: GLD261103C00363000 · **Cboe IV**: 79.9% · **Inverted IV**: 9.2% · **Gap**: 70.7pp (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Contract**: IWM261103C00282000 · **Cboe IV**: 73.8% · **Inverted IV**: 7.5% · **Gap**: 66.3pp (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Contract**: IWM261103P00281000 · **Cboe IV**: 76.5% · **Inverted IV**: 13.4% · **Gap**: 63.1pp (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Contract**: GLD261103C00362000 · **Cboe IV**: 60.3% · **Inverted IV**: 7.0% · **Gap**: 53.2pp (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Contract**: IWM261103P00278000 · **Cboe IV**: 49.7% · **Inverted IV**: 6.5% · **Gap**: 43.2pp (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)

- **The rule this produces:
- read the Cboe IV column as unusable on 0DTE ETF contracts with a sub-$0.05 theoretical value, and read it as reliable elsewhere.** On the liquid single-name rows it is fine —
- AAPL 332.5C (11-04) shows Cboe 37.1% against an inverted 36.8%.
- On the 0DTE ETF rows it is an artifact: IWM 284C shows 123.6% against an inverted 13.0%, a 110.6-point gap on a contract worth $0.005.

- **Yahoo's `impliedVolatility` was used as an independent check, and it agrees with the inversion** (correlation 0.988 against the inverted vol, n = 71), while the Cboe column against the same inversion correlates 0.072 on the 70 rows where Cboe published an IV.
- Note the unit: **Yahoo returns implied volatility as a decimal fraction on this endpoint** (raw 0.2618 = 26.2%), whereas Cboe's `iv` is also a decimal fraction (0.3715 = 37.15%).
- Both are rendered ×100 in this file; reading either as an already-scaled percentage is a 100× error.

**Caveats**

- **Six of the eight underlyings have no session-date expiry** in either tape (TLT, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN), so their windows start 2026-11-04 and their same-day flow is absent from the data rather than from the scan.
- IWM and GLD do carry a 2026-11-03 expiry, and their 0DTE lines dominate the kept set.
- **Cboe's `open_interest` is the prior session's settled OI** while `volume` is today's session, so V/OI is inflated by construction on a gap day.
- Today was a gap day for MSFT (+2.74%), NVDA (+2.29%), AMZN (+2.06%) and AAPL (-1.90%). The OI ≥ 50 slice is published alongside for exactly this reason.
- **Cboe's IV column is an artifact on 0DTE ETF contracts** priced at a penny with a wide spread —
- 15 of the 70 invertible rows diverge by more than 10 vol points, all of them IWM/GLD 0DTE. See the IV reliability section; the inverted vol is quoted there instead.
- **ITM/OTM is side-aware** — a call is ITM below spot, a put above spot. Validated against Yahoo's own `inTheMoney` flag on all 73 kept rows with zero disagreements.
- **The single biggest line is wide and thin.** IWM 280P exp 2026-11-03 traded 195,366 contracts against an open interest of 3,886 (V/OI 50.3) —
- but the quote was 0.33 / 0.72, so the mid is 0.53 and the whole line is worth roughly $104k of premium.
- The call side of the IWM 0DTE cluster is almost entirely $0.005-theoretical prints.
- **No second tape on option volume/OI today** (Nasdaq option-chain 404, second day running). The underlying closes are cross-checked on 8/8; the option volume and open-interest numbers are not.
- **The window is a same-week book.** 36.8% of the chain's real-print volume trades outside the four listed expiries and is invisible to this scan.
